issues.body: `refresh_prohibition` builds ambiguous-deny provenance with `naming_prohibition_ids`, whose filter uses `rule_action_target_match`. That predicate checks only action and target; it omits the assignee match and full constraint classification used by `prohibition_status`. If one prohibition is genuinely ambiguous while another action/target-identical prohibition is assignee-mismatched or definitely false under supplied evidence, the retained deny is annotated with both IDs even though the latter cannot be its source. Calling this "honest over-attribution" is incorrect, and the added provenance tests do not cover this mixed-classification refresh path.
issues.fix_hint: Expose or reuse the evaluator's per-rule three-valued prohibition classification so ambiguous refresh provenance contains only rules classified `Ambiguous` for this request, including assignee and complete constraint evaluation. Add a refresh regression test containing one ambiguous prohibition plus one action/target-identical but assignee-mismatched or definitely-false prohibition, and assert that only the ambiguous rule ID is emitted.
issues.title: Ambiguous refresh still attributes definitely inapplicable prohibitions

verdict.summary: Round 5's major correctness issue remains unchanged. On an ambiguous prohibition refresh, `naming_prohibition_ids` still selects every action/target-compatible prohibition via `rule_action_target_match`, even though the evaluator's actual three-valued classification also considers assignee and constraints. The re-emitted deny can therefore claim provenance from a definitely inapplicable sibling rule. The new tests still do not exercise a mixed ambiguous/definitely-inapplicable refresh case. Progress is stagnant because the same issue remains at the same severity.
